content: 1. For most non-pregnant adults, it is recommended to set a target hemoglobin A1C level of less than 7%. This goal is intended to reduce the risk of diabetes-related complications while maintaining a balance between achieving optimal glycemic control and minimizing the risk of hypoglycemia. 2. In non-pregnant adults who utilize ambulatory glucose profiles or continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), the target should be to maintain a time in range (TIR) of greater than 70%, with time spent below range being less than 4% and time spent below 54 mg/dL being less than 1%. 3. Lower A1C levels may be appropriate for certain individuals, provided they can be achieved without causing significant episodes of hypoglycemia. 4. For individuals at high risk of hypoglycemia or in cases where the burdens of treatment outweigh the benefits, it is advisable to adjust or reduce diabetes medications accordingly. 5. Establishing glycemic goals collaboratively with patients during consultations can enhance their adherence to treatment plans and improve their understanding of diabetes management.
